briefs.headline: Bengals list Burrow with an illness as Risner and Burks miss Thursday's practice
briefs.summary: Quarterback Joe Burrow was listed with an illness on the Bengals' first injury report of the week, published Thursday ahead of Monday night's game at Washington, and the report marked him a full participant; the team's own practice account says he did not go through stretch and that the week's quarterback media session was swapped to Ja'Marr Chase, with Burrow to speak Friday or Saturday. Starting right guard Dalton Risner (knee) and backup linebacker Oren Burks (groin) did not practice and coach Zac Taylor called both day-to-day; cornerback Dax Hill was held out with an illness and defensive tackle Jonathan Allen was given a rest day. Taylor said receiver Tee Higgins, banged up in Sunday night's win over Pittsburgh, is good, and he is not ready to say whether receiver Andrei Iosivas, cornerback Jalen Davis or lineman Brian Parker II, all back at practice off injured reserve last week, will play. ESPN's game preview has Burrow completing 74.7% of his passes, second in the league with 2,795 yards and first with 27 touchdown passes, and the Bengals, seven wins and two losses with five straight wins, third in the NFL at 30.9 points a game with at least 31 in each of the last five. Washington, three wins, five losses and a tie, won 24 to 21 at the Giants last Thursday; kickoff Monday is 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati beats Orlando City 3-1 in the Wild Card and goes to Nashville on Sunday
briefs.summary: FC Cincinnati came from a goal down to win 3-1 at Orlando City in the rain at Inter&Co Stadium on Thursday night in the MLS Cup Playoffs Eastern Conference Wild Card match, per ESPN's match report and key events. Martin Ojeda put Orlando ahead in the 26th minute from Ivan Angulo's through ball; Evander levelled from the penalty spot in the 43rd after Pavel Bucha was fouled by Marco Pasalic, scored again in the 49th from Tom Barlow's pass, and set up Samuel Gidi for the third in the 85th. Orlando had 57.8% of the ball and 27 shots to Cincinnati's 10, but both sides put eight on target; Roman Celentano made six saves and Maxime Crepeau five. Cincinnati now opens a best-of-three Round One series at No. 1 seed Nashville, the Supporters' Shield winners on 77 points, on Sunday at 4 p.m. ET at Geodis Park (FS1, Apple TV); Orlando's Daryl Dike went off injured in the 78th minute and its season is over.

briefs.headline: Wembanyama scores 32 as San Antonio beats the Clippers 124 to 112 without Harper
briefs.summary: San Antonio defeated the LA Clippers 124 to 112 at the Frost Bank Center on Thursday night before 18,532, per ESPN's box score, two nights after Detroit ended its 12-game winning streak. Victor Wembanyama had 32 points on 13 of 26 shooting and 11 rebounds, his seventh 30-point game of the season per the AP account; Stephon Castle had 21 points and 12 assists against eight turnovers, Julian Champagnie 20 with four threes, and San Antonio shot 53%, had 37 assists on 46 baskets and scored 54 points in the paint. The Clippers, four wins and 10 losses, made 17 of 42 threes against a defence that had been allowing a league-low 32.9 attempts a game, with Darius Garland and Brook Lopez scoring 23 each and Max Strus five threes for 18. Dylan Harper, out with the left hip he hurt Tuesday, is expected to miss one to three weeks with a strain, per the AP; Jordan McLaughlin took his rotation minutes and San Antonio outscored Los Angeles by 16 in his 11. San Antonio is 13 wins and three losses, level with the Lakers at the top of the West, and hosts New Orleans on Saturday at 8 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Arena says U.S. Soccer has no clue in its search for Pochettino's successor
briefs.summary: Bruce Arena, the U.S. men's national team's winningest coach and now the San Jose Earthquakes' manager, said Wednesday that U.S. Soccer does not have a clue what it is doing in its search for Mauricio Pochettino's replacement, ESPN reported; Pochettino was confirmed as Manchester United's coach last Friday and left after Tuesday's two-goal win over Haiti in Cincinnati completed an eight-goal aggregate Nations League quarterfinal win. U.S. Soccer has said the search will begin with under-23 coach Steve Cherundolo overseeing a December camp and a friendly against Jamaica next month, per ESPN. Arena, who coached the national team from 1998 to 2006 and again in 2016 and 2017, opposed the Pochettino hiring in 2025 on the grounds that a national team coach should be domestic; his 81 wins are the program record, and his second spell ended with the failure to qualify for the 2018 World Cup.

briefs.headline: Florida beats West Virginia 85-72 in the Players Era third-place game
briefs.summary: No. 1 Florida defeated West Virginia 85-72 at Michelob Ultra Arena in Las Vegas on Thursday afternoon in the third-place game of the Players Era tournament, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story, a day after each had lost a semifinal. The Gators never trailed, led 40-30 at the half after outscoring the Mountaineers 16-2 in fast-break points before the break, and shot 28 of 48 (58%) with 11 of 22 threes, 14 of 22 after halftime, playing without point guard Boogie Fland (right shoulder); Thomas Haugh scored 22 on 7 of 9 with four threes, Urban Klavzar and Alex Condon 17 each and Denzel Aberdeen 12 with five assists, and Florida outrebounded West Virginia 35-23. West Virginia forced 18 turnovers and turned them into 22 points and got within three in the second half, but shot 24 of 56 and 7 of 22 from three; Miles Sadler had 18 on 5 of 17 a day after his 34, Finley Bizjack 14 and Javan Buchanan 12. The Mountaineers are 4-2 with a season-low 72 points and consecutive losses, and next play North Carolina in Charlotte on Friday, Nov. 27, at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN; Florida is 6-1. Houston defeated Kansas 92-83 in Thursday night's final.

briefs.headline: Onosato forces out Wakamotoharu to share the Kyushu lead at 11 wins with two days left
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato forced out maegashira (rank-and-file) 7 Wakamotoharu by yorikiri (frontal force-out) on day 13 of the Kyushu basho (tournament) in Fukuoka on Friday, ending the maegashira's 10-bout winning run and leaving the two level at 11 wins and two losses, per the Japan Sumo Association's tournament leaders page; the SumoDB results table has Onosato leading their head-to-head series nine bouts to three. Both chasers at 10 wins lost as well: sekiwake (third-highest rank) Atamifuji was forced out by maegashira 8 Roga, and maegashira 7 Kinbozan was forced out by ozeki (champion) Kirishima, so Atamifuji and Kinbozan stand at 10 wins and three losses, with Kirishima, Roga, maegashira 1 Asanoyama, who forced down Ura, maegashira 11 Takanosho and maegashira 11 Asahakuryu a win further back at nine and four. Yokozuna Hoshoryu threw down ozeki Aonishiki from behind by okurinage (rear throw) and ozeki Kotozakura thrust down Gonoyama by tsukiotoshi, so both reached eight wins and five losses, a kachi-koshi (winning record), while Aonishiki fell to six and seven and must win his last two to avoid a make-koshi (losing record). The day 14 pairings on Saturday have Onosato against Kinbozan, Wakamotoharu against Aonishiki, Atamifuji against Kirishima and ozeki Kotozakura against yokozuna Hoshoryu. In juryo (the second division) Wakatakakage pushed out Kagayaki and leads alone at 12 wins and one loss, with Asahifuji at 11 and two. The final day is Sunday, Nov. 22.

briefs.headline: Houston beats Kansas 92-83 for the Players Era title after leading by 24
briefs.summary: No. 8 Houston defeated No. 11 Kansas 92-83 in the Players Era championship game in Las Vegas on Thursday night, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story, opening with a 15-3 run, leading 54-34 at the half and by as many as 24 before Kansas got within 81-76 with 2:33 left on two Leroy Blyden Jr. free throws; Dedan Thomas Jr. answered with a layup and a floater. Mercy Miller scored 21 for the Cougars, Delrecco Gillespie 19 and Thomas 16 with eight assists, and Houston outrebounded Kansas 25-15 in the first half with 11 offensive boards. Freshman Tyran Stokes, who sat out Wednesday's semifinal against West Virginia with a bone bruise, had 22 points and 11 rebounds for Kansas, with Dennis Parker Jr. scoring 18, Blyden 17 and Tre White 13. Houston is 6-0 a day after beating No. 1 Florida; Kansas is 5-1. Notre Dame took fifth place 78-73 over Auburn and Rutgers seventh 89-70 over UNLV.

briefs.headline: Texans beat the Colts 26-3 on Thursday night for their first home win of the season
briefs.summary: C.J. Stroud threw for 194 yards and three touchdowns and Houston defeated Indianapolis 26-3 on Thursday night, per ESPN's box score and the AP account, the Texans' first home win after four home losses, with the stadium roof open for the first time since 2024. Nico Collins caught a 42-yard score late in the first quarter, Kamari Lassiter intercepted Daniel Jones on the first play of the second, Kayshon Boutte finished the 85-yard drive that followed, and Will Anderson Jr. sacked Jones in the end zone for a safety in the third; Anderson leads the NFL with 11.5 sacks. Indianapolis played without injured cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward and scored only a first-quarter field goal. Houston is 4-6, a week after losing 27-24 at Cleveland, and Indianapolis is 3-8.

briefs.headline: Grizzlies win a fifth straight and Lillard scores 33 in his return to Milwaukee
briefs.summary: Memphis defeated short-handed Golden State 126 to 98 on Thursday for a fifth straight win behind Jaylen Wells's 22 points, per ESPN's scoreboard, moving to 12 wins and four losses, one game off the top of the West, while the Warriors have lost five in a row and are eight and eight. Portland won 124 to 114 at Milwaukee with Damian Lillard scoring 33 in his first game back in the city he left; the Bucks have lost 12 straight and are one and 15, the league's worst record. New York held off Minnesota 102 to 99 behind Karl-Anthony Towns's 22 points and 12 rebounds against his former team, dropping the Timberwolves to 11 and five.

waters.reading: 97.3 cfs, 1.62 feet at 5:15 a.m., steady on flow and stage against 97.3 cfs and 1.62 feet in the fetcher's 24-hour comparison.
waters.working: The gauge at Dyer reads 97.3 cfs and 1.62 feet, the same two numbers as the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and a hair under the 99.1 cfs and 1.63 feet Thursday's paper carried, so Wednesday's small rise has settled straight back to the late-autumn base flow the river has held all week. At 97 cfs and clear it is a long-leader, small-fly problem, with the fish on the pocket-water lies and the tailouts rather than the seams, and after another cold night the midday hours fish best once the sun is on the water. A size 18 to 20 midge or a small Blue-winged Olive nymph under a soft indicator on a long leader through the slower pockets and the tailouts is the pattern, a stonefly nymph as the point fly in the deeper plunge pools where the larger fish hold in cold water, and a sculpin pattern swung tight to the undercut banks in the first and last hour of light.

waters.working: Normal pool with ordinary bank access, steady on the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and 15 hundredths under the 25.01 Thursday's paper carried, so the upper gauge is back where it sat Wednesday, inside a quarter-foot band it has held all week. The wing dams and the riprap are showing rock and the water is clear enough to fish structure rather than the slack behind it: shad are the forage, so a white or shad-pattern swimbait or a lipless crankbait worked down the face of the wing dams and along the riprap is the pattern, slowed down for water that saw another cold night, with a jig and crawfish on the slack side of the lock wall for the fish holding off the current. The R.C. Byrd tailwater itself is not gauged; this is the pool side.
waters.source: USGS 03201500 (Ohio River at Point Pleasant); config.SPORTSMAN_WATERS

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.26 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.43 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.3 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool and steady, three hundredths over the 26.23 Thursday's paper carried and 17 hundredths under the fetcher's 24-hour comparison, so the lower gauge keeps moving a few inches either way around 26 feet while the upper gauge holds near 25. Below the dam the pattern is the structure the dam makes: skipjack and shad stack in the current below the gates, and a spoon or a heavy jig worked in the churn, or a live skipjack drifted along the current seams off the lock wall, is the hybrid and catfish setup; the riprap along the Huntington bank fishes a crawfish-colour jig on the slack side where the bank current breaks. Huntington is the downstream bracket, 30-odd river miles below the dam, not the tailwater reading, which the Corps publish and this pipeline cannot fetch.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: high 4:01 AM at 3.5 ft, low 10:34 AM at 0.7 ft, high 4:21 PM at 3.4 ft, low 10:48 PM at 0.2 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 3:15 AM at 4.4 ft, low 9:27 AM at 0.7 ft, high 3:28 PM at 4.0 ft, low 9:30 PM at 0.3 ft. Water 58.8F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon waxing gibbous, 81% illuminated, 10.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 4:01 AM and 4:21 PM in the sound.
waters.working: All eight events land inside Friday on both stations, the table 50 to 60 minutes later than Thursday's. The sound lags the surf by 46 minutes on the overnight high, 67 on the morning low, 53 on the afternoon high and 78 on the evening low, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills; the afternoon flood climbs 2.7 feet from the 10:34 low to the 4:21 high and the evening ebb drops 3.2 feet to the 10:48 low at 0.2 feet, the lowest low of the week, and at waxing gibbous, 81% and 10.5 days the moon is about four days short of full, which the file's age puts on Tuesday, so the swings are building through the week toward the spring tides. The water at Beaufort read 58.8F at 5:30 a.m., up 1.4 degrees from Thursday's reading. The NWS active-alerts feed for North Carolina, read at 5:51 a.m., carried no product for the state: no frost advisory, rip current or beach hazards statement. The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report, a monthly, is dated Nov. 1 and is 19 days old, so it is the month's pattern and not this morning's conditions: East Coast Sports reports the piers taking a few big red drum of 32 inches and up on the north end, smaller reds and the occasional speckled trout in the sound with the focus shifting to almost exclusive trout action as the water cools; Native Son says the 5-to-8-foot seams in the main creeks are the trout target and cut bait the best bet for scattered reds; Speckled Specialist reports live shrimp under a cork in 4 to 16 feet of water, 3/16-ounce jig heads with a soft plastic for artificials and black drum to 18 inches on the same floated shrimp over structure; Carolina Flats has topwater for locating trout early, deeper holes later and the reds in a last blitz on the oyster and grass banks before the bait thins; Jolly Roger Pier reports scattered speckled trout, Virginia mullet and spot at night and thick bluefish early; Surf City Pier has pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom. Tied to today's table and a sound still in the 50s, the 10:34 low falls in the cold middle of the morning and the window is the top of the flood and the first of the ebb, roughly 1 to 5 p.m., once the sun has been on the flats: trout in the 5-to-8-foot creek-channel seams and along the ICWW channel edge on a 3/16-ounce jig head and a small soft plastic worked slowly, or a live shrimp under a popping cork drifted over the oyster bars at the creek mouths as the water starts to leave the grass after 4:21. Red drum want the last of the fall, roughly 8 p.m. to the 10:48 low, which is well into dark on a 0.2-foot bottom that will drain the creek mouths hard: cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges, or a soft plastic on the oyster and grass banks in the last of the light; the flooded-grass window for a weedless gold spoon is the hour before the 4:21 high. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel on the last of the flood; bluefish are the beach fish on a metal jig in the early morning. Flounder are release only.
waters.source: NOAA CO-OPS 8657813 (sound), 8657419 (surf), 8656483 (Beaufort); Fisherman's Post, Topsail/Sneads Ferry November 2026 report (Nov. 1); reference/topsail-fishing.md seasonal calendar; NWS; NCDMF
